subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw status falsely reports openclaw-mem0 memory as unavailable when the live gateway plugin is working

question: Should memory status truth come from a live gateway runtime-health contract, the current local plugin manager status path, or be folded into the broader passive-status work?
rationale: The remaining fix shape changes the status/doctor contract for memory plugins and overlaps an open closing PR plus a broader local side-effect issue, so automation should not choose the permanent product boundary alone.

options.title: Repair or replace the linked PR with a runtime-health contract
options.body: Add a maintainer-approved runtime-vs-embedding status contract and close this issue only after the linked implementation path is resolved or replaced.

options.title: Keep the partial mitigation and close the linked PR
options.body: Accept `not checked` plus `status --all` local plugin status as the intended behavior and close the implementation PR as no longer wanted.

options.title: Move all remaining work to the broader status-side-effect issue
options.body: Treat this issue as covered by the broader passive-status contract at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599 and use that item as the canonical remaining work.

recommendation.title: Repair or replace the linked PR with a runtime-health contract
recommendation.body: Add a maintainer-approved runtime-vs-embedding status contract and close this issue only after the linked implementation path is resolved or replaced.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the memory-runtime plugin refactor and current custom memory status handling, making them the best available owner for the status/plugin boundary decision.
